default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-778.title: Minute-of-day seasonal sign
E-778.hypothesis: If the same minute of the day closed the same colour in most of the last 20 sessions, recurring scheduled flows (fixings, rebalancing, opening of other markets) at that clock time may repeat; follow the habit.

E-779.title: Seasonal-path deviation fade
E-779.hypothesis: Compare the day's return from the open with the average path of the last 20 sessions at the same minute; a large excess over that typical path is overshoot against the usual flow, so fade it.

E-780.title: Equal-close stall after a move
E-780.hypothesis: Bars closing exactly on the previous close show the aggressors stepping away after a move; the prior direction resumes once the pause passes.

E-781.title: Session heavy-volume bar range break
E-781.hypothesis: The session's highest-volume bar so far marks where most positions were built; a close beyond its range leaves those holders offside and they must exit in the break direction.

E-782.title: Price-impact spike fade
E-782.hypothesis: A move that needed little volume per point (impact far above the usual at that minute) is a liquidity vacuum, not conviction; it tends to retrace once liquidity returns.

E-785.title: VWAP side at clock marks
E-785.hypothesis: At round clock marks, being clearly on one side of the session VWAP means the volume-weighted average holder is on the other side and the drift keeps that side; follow it.

E-786.title: Tweezer reversal at a window extreme
E-786.hypothesis: Two consecutive bars stopping at the same high (low) after the first was strong marks a defended level at the window extreme; fade the second bar's reversal colour.

E-787.title: Heavy-volume bar trap
E-787.hypothesis: A heavy-volume directional bar fully retraced by the next bar's close through its open traps the aggressors; the retrace direction continues.

E-784.title: PTAX window move fade
E-784.hypothesis: Dollar flows around the four PTAX fixing windows (10, 11, 12, 13h) push the price temporarily; after the window ends the push is not information and tends to fade.
